mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 9.5% signals economic weakness and reduced corporate profitability expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 9.5, or the Rank IC is negative over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in CPIAUCSL and stable FEDFUNDS (no rate hikes) signal the Federal Reserve is behind the curve on inflation, leading to higher real interest rates and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with delayed policy response
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises and FEDFUNDS is stable, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, high industrial production (INDPRO) signals economic overheating and impending monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of late-cycle expansion periods with INDPRO above 95, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strengthening consumer demand and economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as market participants anticipate improved corporate earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST rises, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% over three months signals weakening consumer spending, reducing corporate revenue expectations and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS declines > 0.5%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Weak employment growth (PAYEMS) combined with high unemployment (UNRATE) signals a deteriorating labor market, reducing consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS growth is low and UNRATE is high, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes, rising CPIAUCSL signals persistent inflationary pressures that prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of high inflation periods with rising CPIAUCSL, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.
